title: Serialize expense allocation generation and explicit void against source changes
description: Stage3 core finance closure. Use genuine authenticated existing ERP permissions; no new user grants or anonymous/admin fallback. Retain inventory source document audit and original failed logs. Run relevant unit tests and safe Release build/full unit suite. Real SQL must target exact (localdb)\NEWERP_AutoAcceptance with IntegratedSecurity and a new GUID-owned NEWERP_AUTOTEST database; reject existing/wrong target before access, never drop/reset or read production settings. Include two independent connection race tests where applicable. Build completion never implies stage acceptance.
acceptance_criteria: Implement one atomic transaction and compatible source/loading/expense lock order for batch generation, explicit void and source expense commercial edits/delete; recheck live ERP385 expense authorization and authoritative source amount/currency/customer/participant bases under locks. Prevent simultaneous generation from consuming the same source twice or duplicate same-source effective batch. Void remains explicit with reason and original audit; cancelled/deleted/changed source cannot produce stale new evidence. Preserve exact currency rounding, residual distribution, zero/invalid basis denial and original generated expense snapshots without inventing balances or rewriting loading/settlement amounts.

Make legacy allocation generation duplicate check and document number reservation atomic under compatible existing number/source key locking; do not treat free-text RefNo as authoritative source identity. Two concurrent equivalent legacy requests create at most one complete set of expenses and distinct requests cannot collide on expense numbers. Any invalid row, stale permission, source conflict or database failure rolls back entire generated set/batch, audit and number reservation as supported by existing service. No physical history deletion, new grants, arbitrary SQL or production migrations. Actual SQL two-connection duplicate legacy generation, source edit/delete vs batch generation, generate vs void and participant update vs generation plus live permission denial and exact amount totals; meaningful unit and safe Release tests, browser evidence or accurate blocker.
